CHAPTER 12 — संवादलेखनम् (SAMVADALEKHANAM — DIALOGUE WRITING)

Introduction — संवादः किम्?

The word संवादः (samvādaḥ) is formed from सम् (sam = together, well) + वादः (vādaḥ = speaking) — 'speaking together', i.e. a conversation or dialogue. संवादलेखनम् is the art of WRITING such a conversation in Sanskrit: two (or more) people exchanging greetings, questions and answers in short, natural sentences. Dialogue writing is one of the most useful composition skills in the NIOS Senior Secondary Sanskrit (309) course, because it turns your grammar — verb forms, pronouns, question words — into living speech. A student who can write a good संवाद can also SPEAK simple Sanskrit, which is the real goal of language learning (संस्कृतसम्भाषणम्).

A good written dialogue has five qualities: (1) it begins and ends with a proper अभिवादनम् (greeting/leave-taking); (2) the sentences are SHORT and natural, as people actually speak; (3) questions and answers alternate in a logical flow (प्रश्नोत्तरप्रवाहः); (4) polite forms such as भवान्/भवती and the courteous imperative (उपविशतु, वदतु) are used correctly; and (5) the vocabulary suits the situation — school words in a school dialogue, market words in a market dialogue.

अभिवादनम् — Greetings and polite forms

Every Sanskrit conversation opens with a greeting. The commonest are: नमस्ते / नमो नमः (salutation, usable at any time of day), सुप्रभातम् (good morning), शुभरात्रिः (good night), स्वागतम् (welcome), and at parting पुनर्मिलामः ('we shall meet again'). Other everyday courtesy words: धन्यवादः (thank you), क्षम्यताम् (pardon me / excuse me), अस्तु (all right, okay), आम् (yes), न / नहि (no), चिन्ता मास्तु (do not worry), साधु / उत्तमम् (very good / excellent), चिरात् दर्शनम् ('seen after a long time' — long time no see).

The most important politeness rule concerns the pronouns भवान् (you — for a man, respectful) and भवती (you — for a woman, respectful). Although they MEAN 'you', grammatically they are THIRD-person pronouns, so the verb must be third person singular (प्रथमपुरुष एकवचन):
  • भवान् कुत्र गच्छति? — Where are you (sir) going? (गच्छति, NOT गच्छसि)
  • भवती किं पठति? — What are you (madam) reading?
  • भवान् कथम् अस्ति? — How are you? Answer: अहं कुशली अस्मि (m.) / अहं कुशलिनी अस्मि (f.) — I am well.
Only with the informal pronoun त्वम् (you — intimate, for friends and juniors) does the verb take the second person: त्वं कुत्र गच्छसि? The genitive (possessive) of भवान् is भवतः ('your', of a man) and of भवती is भवत्याः ('your', of a woman): भवतः नाम किम्? — What is your name? Politeness is also shown by the courteous imperative (लोट्लकार, third person singular): उपविशतु (please sit), आगच्छतु (please come), वदतु (please speak), ददातु (please give), गृह्णातु (please take), पिबतु (please drink), करोतु (please do).

प्रश्नोत्तरप्रवाहः — Question words that drive a dialogue

A dialogue moves forward on questions. The key प्रश्नवाचक (interrogative) words are: किम् (what), कः / का (who — m./f.), कुत्र (where), कदा (when), कथम् (how), किमर्थम् (why / for what purpose), कति (how many), कियत् (how much). Examples: भवतः नाम किम्? (What is your name?) भवान् कुत्र वसति? (Where do you live?) विद्यालयः कदा आरभते? (When does school begin?) एतत् कथम् अभवत्? (How did this happen?) एकस्य किलोपरिमाणस्य कति मूल्यम्? (What is the price of one kilo?) A question with वा at the end expects yes/no: गृहकार्यं कृतवान् वा? (Have you done the homework?)

आदर्शसंवादाः — Model dialogues (original, with English explanation)

(1) शिक्षक-छात्रयोः संवादः — Teacher and student

छात्रः — नमस्ते गुरो!
शिक्षकः — नमस्ते वत्स! भवान् कथम् अस्ति?
छात्रः — अहं कुशली अस्मि। भवान् कथम् अस्ति?
शिक्षकः — अहम् अपि कुशली। भवान् इदानीं किं पठति?
छात्रः — अहं संस्कृतं पठामि।
शिक्षकः — उत्तमम्! भवान् कदा पठति?
छात्रः — अहं प्रातःकाले पठामि।
शिक्षकः — गृहकार्यं कृतवान् वा?
छात्रः — आम् गुरो, कृतवान्।
शिक्षकः — साधु साधु! सदा एवं करोतु।
छात्रः — धन्यवादः गुरो!

English explanation: The student greets the teacher with नमस्ते and the vocative गुरो! (O teacher — सम्बोधन of गुरु). The teacher addresses the boy as वत्स (child/dear). Note the politeness grammar throughout: the teacher says भवान् ... पठति (third-person verb with भवान्), while the student, speaking of himself, uses the first person पठामि. The yes/no question गृहकार्यं कृतवान् वा? is answered with आम् (yes). The dialogue closes with praise (साधु साधु), a courteous imperative (करोतु) and thanks (धन्यवादः).

(2) मित्रयोः संवादः — Between two friends

रमेशः — नमस्ते सुरेश!
सुरेशः — नमो नमः रमेश! चिरात् दर्शनम्!
रमेशः — आम्, अहं ग्रामं गतवान् आसम्। भवान् कुत्र आसीत्?
सुरेशः — अहम् अत्रैव आसम्। श्वः किं करिष्यति भवान्?
रमेशः — श्वः अहं क्रीडाङ्गणं गमिष्यामि। भवान् अपि आगच्छतु।
सुरेशः — अस्तु, अहम् अपि आगमिष्यामि। कदा गमिष्यावः?
रमेशः — सायङ्काले पञ्चवादने।
सुरेशः — उत्तमम्। तर्हि श्वः मिलावः।
रमेशः — अस्तु, पुनर्मिलामः।

English explanation: Friends may greet each other with नमस्ते or नमो नमः. चिरात् दर्शनम् means 'long time no see'. Notice the tenses: गतवान् आसम् (I had gone), आसीत् (was), and the future गमिष्यामि / आगमिष्यामि (I will go / come). कदा गमिष्यावः? uses the DUAL first person (उत्तमपुरुष द्विवचन) — 'when shall we two go?' — and मिलावः 'we two shall meet'. Time is told with सायङ्काले पञ्चवादने (in the evening, at five o'clock). The parting phrase पुनर्मिलामः ends the dialogue politely.

(3) आपणे क्रेता-विक्रेतयोः संवादः — Buyer and seller in a shop

क्रेता — नमस्ते महोदय!
विक्रेता — नमस्ते! स्वागतम्। भवान् किम् इच्छति?
क्रेता — मम फलानि आवश्यकानि। आम्रफलानि सन्ति वा?
विक्रेता — आम्, सन्ति। नूतनानि मधुराणि च आम्रफलानि सन्ति।
क्रेता — एकस्य किलोपरिमाणस्य कति मूल्यम्?
विक्रेता — अशीतिः रूप्यकाणि महोदय।
क्रेता — मूल्यम् अधिकम् अस्ति। किञ्चित् न्यूनं करोतु।
विक्रेता — अस्तु, सप्ततिः रूप्यकाणि ददातु।
क्रेता — साधु। द्वे किलोपरिमाणे ददातु।
विक्रेता — गृह्णातु महोदय। धन्यवादः।
क्रेता — धन्यवादः। पुनः आगमिष्यामि।

English explanation: क्रेता = buyer, विक्रेता = seller, आपणः = shop. The respectful address महोदय (sir) is used on both sides. The seller welcomes the customer (स्वागतम्) and asks भवान् किम् इच्छति? (What do you want? — इच्छति, third person, with भवान्). The price question is एकस्य किलोपरिमाणस्य कति मूल्यम्? (How much for one kilo?), answered in रूप्यकाणि (rupees). Bargaining uses the courteous imperative: न्यूनं करोतु (please reduce), ददातु (please give), गृह्णातु (please take). Both close with धन्यवादः.

(4) चिकित्सक-रुग्णयोः संवादः — Doctor and patient

रुग्णः — नमस्ते वैद्यमहोदय!
चिकित्सकः — नमस्ते! उपविशतु। भवतः का पीडा?
रुग्णः — ह्यः रात्रौ आरभ्य मम शिरोवेदना ज्वरः च अस्ति।
चिकित्सकः — मुखम् उद्घाटयतु। ... आम्, भवतः शरीरे ज्वरः अस्ति। भोजनं कृतवान् वा?
रुग्णः — न महोदय, क्षुधा एव नास्ति।
चिकित्सकः — चिन्ता मास्तु। एतत् औषधं दिने त्रिवारं स्वीकरोतु। उष्णं जलं पिबतु। विश्रामं च करोतु।
रुग्णः — अस्तु महोदय। पुनः कदा आगच्छामि?
चिकित्सकः — त्रिदिनानन्तरम् आगच्छतु।
रुग्णः — धन्यवादः महोदय।
चिकित्सकः — शीघ्रं स्वस्थः भवतु।

English explanation: चिकित्सकः / वैद्यः = doctor, रुग्णः = patient. The doctor politely seats the patient (उपविशतु) and asks भवतः का पीडा? — 'What is YOUR trouble?' — where भवतः is the genitive of भवान्. The patient describes symptoms: शिरोवेदना (headache), ज्वरः (fever), क्षुधा नास्ति (no appetite), ह्यः रात्रौ आरभ्य (since last night). The doctor's instructions are all courteous imperatives: उद्घाटयतु (open), स्वीकरोतु (take), पिबतु (drink), करोतु (do/take rest); दिने त्रिवारम् = three times a day. The blessing शीघ्रं स्वस्थः भवतु (get well soon) is the natural close.

व्याकरणम् — Grammar for conversation

(A) लट्लकारः (present tense) is the backbone of dialogue, since conversation mostly happens in the present. For the root पठ् (to read): प्रथमपुरुष (3rd person) पठति / पठतः / पठन्ति; मध्यमपुरुष (2nd person) पठसि / पठथः / पठथ; उत्तमपुरुष (1st person) पठामि / पठावः / पठामः. In dialogue: सः पठति (he reads), भवान् पठति (you, sir, read — third person!), त्वं पठसि (you read — informal), अहं पठामि (I read), आवां पठावः (we two read), वयं पठामः (we read).

(B) सम्बोधनम् (vocative — calling someone) opens many dialogue lines: हे राम! (O Rama!), हे मित्र! (O friend!), भोः (a general calling word — भो मित्र!), गुरो! (O teacher — vocative of गुरु), वत्स! (dear child), महोदय! (sir), महोदये! (madam), आर्य! (noble sir).

(C) प्रश्नवाचकशब्दाः in use: किम् (what), कः/का (who), कुत्र (where), कदा (when), कथम् (how), किमर्थम् (why), कति (how many), कियत् (how much) — and the tag वा for yes/no questions. A complete question-answer pair: प्रश्नः — भवान् कुत्र वसति? उत्तरम् — अहं दिल्लीनगरे वसामि।

(D) Layout rules for the examination: write the title (e.g. मित्रयोः संवादः) at the top; write each speaker's name followed by a dash (—) at the left; keep 8-12 exchanges; begin with a greeting and end with leave-taking (धन्यवादः / पुनर्मिलामः / शुभं भवतु); keep sentences short; and check every भवान्/भवती sentence for its third-person verb.

SUMMARY (सारांश)

संवादलेखनम् (सम् + वादः) is the skill of writing natural Sanskrit conversation. A good dialogue opens with अभिवादनम् (नमस्ते, नमो नमः, सुप्रभातम्), moves through a logical question-answer flow driven by प्रश्नवाचक words (किम्, कुत्र, कदा, कथम्, किमर्थम्, कति), uses situation-appropriate everyday vocabulary, and closes with courtesy (धन्यवादः, पुनर्मिलामः). Its central grammar rule: the respectful pronouns भवान् (m.) and भवती (f.) take a THIRD-person singular verb (भवान् गच्छति), unlike informal त्वम् which takes the second person (त्वं गच्छसि); politeness is completed by courteous imperatives (उपविशतु, वदतु, ददातु) and proper सम्बोधन (गुरो!, महोदय!, हे मित्र!). The four model dialogues — teacher-student, two friends, buyer-seller, doctor-patient — show these principles at work in daily situations. Practise by writing your own 8-12 line dialogues on familiar scenes; that is the surest road to speaking Sanskrit.

topics.name: संवादलेखनम् — Meaning and Qualities of Dialogue Writing
topics.description: What संवादः (सम् + वादः, 'speaking together') means; what संवादलेखनम् is as a composition skill; and the five qualities of a good written dialogue — greeting, short natural sentences, question-answer flow, polite forms and situation-appropriate vocabulary.

topics.description: Opening and closing a dialogue with नमस्ते, नमो नमः, सुप्रभातम्, स्वागतम्, पुनर्मिलामः, and everyday courtesy words such as धन्यवादः, क्षम्यताम्, अस्तु, आम्, चिन्ता मास्तु and चिरात् दर्शनम्.

topics.description: The respectful pronouns भवान् (m.) and भवती (f.) meaning 'you' but taking a third-person singular verb (भवान् गच्छति), contrasted with informal त्वम् (+2nd person verb); genitives भवतः / भवत्याः; and courteous imperatives उपविशतु, वदतु, ददातु.

topics.name: दैनन्दिनशब्दावली — Everyday Conversational Vocabulary
topics.description: Vocabulary for daily situations — school (विद्यालयः, गृहकार्यम्), market (आपणः, क्रेता, विक्रेता, मूल्यम्, रूप्यकम्), clinic (चिकित्सकः, रुग्णः, औषधम्, ज्वरः), and time words (अद्य, श्वः, ह्यः, प्रातःकाले, सायङ्काले).

chapter_summary.intro: This is the NIOS Senior Secondary Sanskrit (309) summary for Chapter 12. It explains what संवादलेखनम् (dialogue writing) is, teaches the greetings and polite forms that open and close a Sanskrit conversation — especially the rule that भवान्/भवती take a third-person verb — presents the question words that drive a dialogue, and walks through four model dialogues (teacher-student, friends, shop, clinic) with their grammar and layout conventions.

sections.heading: What dialogue writing is and what makes it good
bullets: संवादः = सम् (together) + वादः (speaking): a conversation; संवादलेखनम् is the composition skill of writing one in Sanskrit.
A good dialogue opens with a greeting, ends with leave-taking, and in between alternates questions and answers logically (प्रश्नोत्तरप्रवाहः).
Sentences must be short and natural — written as people actually speak — and the vocabulary must fit the situation (school, market, clinic).
Exam layout: title on top (e.g. मित्रयोः संवादः), speaker's name + dash at the left of each line, about 8-12 exchanges.

sections.heading: Greetings and courtesy phrases
bullets: Opening greetings: नमस्ते / नमो नमः (any time), सुप्रभातम् (good morning), स्वागतम् (welcome); closing: धन्यवादः, पुनर्मिलामः, शुभं भवतु.
Everyday courtesy: क्षम्यताम् (pardon me), अस्तु (all right), आम् (yes), न/नहि (no), चिन्ता मास्तु (don't worry), साधु/उत्तमम् (very good).
चिरात् दर्शनम् = 'long time no see' — used when friends meet after a gap.
How-are-you exchange: भवान् कथम् अस्ति? → अहं कुशली अस्मि (m.) / कुशलिनी अस्मि (f.).

sections.heading: The भवान्/भवती rule and courteous imperatives
bullets: भवान् (m.) and भवती (f.) mean 'you' respectfully but are grammatically THIRD person: भवान् कुत्र गच्छति? — never गच्छसि.
Informal त्वम् takes the second person: त्वं कुत्र गच्छसि? — used only with close friends and juniors.
Genitive forms: भवतः नाम किम्? (your name, of a man), भवत्याः नाम किम्? (of a woman).
Politeness is completed with third-person courteous imperatives: उपविशतु, आगच्छतु, वदतु, ददातु, गृह्णातु, पिबतु, करोतु.

sections.heading: Question words that drive the flow
bullets: किम् (what), कः/का (who), कुत्र (where), कदा (when), कथम् (how), किमर्थम् (why), कति (how many), कियत् (how much).
Yes/no questions take the tag वा: गृहकार्यं कृतवान् वा? — answered आम् (yes) or न (no).
Every question should get a matching, complete answer: भवान् कुत्र वसति? → अहं दिल्लीनगरे वसामि।
Price is asked with कति मूल्यम्?; time with कदा?; manner with कथम्?

sections.heading: The four model dialogues and their grammar
bullets: Teacher-student: सम्बोधन गुरो!/वत्स!, the भवान्+3rd-person rule, yes/no tag वा, praise साधु साधु and closing धन्यवादः.
Friends: नमो नमः, चिरात् दर्शनम्, future tense गमिष्यामि, and the dual गमिष्यावः/मिलावः ('we two').
Shop: क्रेता/विक्रेता/आपणः, price bargaining with कति मूल्यम्? and न्यूनं करोतु, courteous ददातु/गृह्णातु.
Clinic: भवतः का पीडा? (genitive भवतः), symptoms ज्वरः/शिरोवेदना, prescriptions with स्वीकरोतु/पिबतु, blessing शीघ्रं स्वस्थः भवतु.
लट्लकार of पठ्: पठति-पठतः-पठन्ति / पठसि-पठथः-पठथ / पठामि-पठावः-पठामः — the backbone of conversation.

key_takeaways: संवादलेखनम् (सम् + वादः) is the art of writing natural Sanskrit conversation — short sentences, logical question-answer flow, correct courtesy.
Every dialogue opens with a greeting (नमस्ते / नमो नमः / सुप्रभातम्) and closes with leave-taking (धन्यवादः, पुनर्मिलामः).
भवान्/भवती mean 'you' respectfully but take a THIRD-person singular verb: भवान् गच्छति — the single most tested rule of this chapter.
Informal त्वम् takes the second person (त्वं गच्छसि); genitives of the polite pronouns are भवतः (m.) and भवत्याः (f.).
Questions are framed with किम्, कः/का, कुत्र, कदा, कथम्, किमर्थम्, कति, कियत्, and yes/no questions with the tag वा.
Courteous imperatives (उपविशतु, वदतु, ददातु, गृह्णातु) and vocatives (गुरो!, महोदय!, हे मित्र!) give the dialogue its polite tone.
The four model situations — teacher-student, friends, buyer-seller, doctor-patient — supply reusable patterns for composing your own 8-12 line dialogues.

glossary.definition: A conversation or dialogue; from सम् (together) + वादः (speaking) — 'speaking together'.
Dialogue writing — the composition skill of writing a natural Sanskrit conversation between two or more speakers.
Greeting or salutation that opens a dialogue — नमस्ते, नमो नमः, सुप्रभातम्, स्वागतम्.
Respectful pronouns for 'you' (masculine/feminine) that take a third-person singular verb: भवान् गच्छति, भवती पठति.
The informal pronoun 'you', used with close friends and juniors; takes a second-person verb: त्वं गच्छसि.
The genitive ('your') forms of भवान् and भवती respectively: भवतः नाम किम्? — What is your name?
Interrogative (question) words: किम् what, कः/का who, कुत्र where, कदा when, कथम् how, किमर्थम् why, कति how many, कियत् how much.
The tag placed at the end of a sentence to make a yes/no question: गृहकार्यं कृतवान् वा?
The present tense — the backbone of conversation; e.g. पठति (he/she reads), पठामि (I read), पठामः (we read).
The vocative — the form used to call or address someone: हे मित्र!, गुरो!, वत्स!, महोदय!, भोः.
'Thank you' — the standard word of thanks that often closes a Sanskrit dialogue.
'We shall meet again' — the common parting phrase at the end of a conversation.
Buyer and seller — the two speakers of a market dialogue; the shop itself is आपणः and the price is मूल्यम्.
Doctor and patient — the speakers of a clinic dialogue; medicine is औषधम्, fever is ज्वरः.
'Well, in good health' (masculine/feminine) — the standard answer to भवान्/भवती कथम् अस्ति?

worksheet.title: Worksheet — संवादलेखनम् (NIOS Sanskrit 309, Chapter 12)
worksheet.instructions: Attempt all questions. Write Sanskrit in Devanagari and explanations in English. Remember: भवान्/भवती always take a third-person singular verb. Refer to the model dialogues in the lesson where needed.

questions.question: What does संवादः literally mean? Break the word into its parts and define संवादलेखनम् in one sentence.
questions.answer: संवादः = सम् (together, well) + वादः (speaking) — 'speaking together', i.e. a conversation. संवादलेखनम् is the composition skill of writing such a conversation in Sanskrit — two or more speakers exchanging greetings, questions and answers in short natural sentences.
questions.explanation: Definition by word-formation plus the composition-skill sense.

questions.question: Give the Sanskrit expression for each: (a) good morning (b) welcome (c) thank you (d) we shall meet again.
questions.explanation: Core greeting and leave-taking vocabulary of the chapter.

questions.question: Correct the errors in these sentences and explain the rule: (a) भवान् कुत्र गच्छसि? (b) त्वं किं पठति?
questions.answer: (a) भवान् कुत्र गच्छति? — भवान् is grammatically third person, so the verb must be third person singular (गच्छति), not second person (गच्छसि). (b) त्वं किं पठसि? — त्वम् takes a second-person verb (पठसि), not third person (पठति).
questions.explanation: The central agreement rule: भवान्/भवती + 3rd person; त्वम् + 2nd person.

questions.question: Fill each blank with the right प्रश्नवाचक word (किम् / कुत्र / कदा / कथम्): (a) भवान् ____ वसति? (I live in Delhi.) (b) विद्यालयः ____ आरभते? (At ten o'clock.) (c) भवतः नाम ____? (My name is Rama.)
questions.answer: (a) कुत्र — भवान् कुत्र वसति? (asking where) (b) कदा — विद्यालयः कदा आरभते? (asking when) (c) किम् — भवतः नाम किम्? (asking what)
questions.explanation: Choose the question word by looking at what the answer supplies: place → कुत्र, time → कदा, thing/name → किम्.

questions.question: Give the English meaning of each market/clinic word: आपणः, क्रेता, विक्रेता, मूल्यम्, औषधम्, ज्वरः.
questions.answer: आपणः = shop; क्रेता = buyer; विक्रेता = seller; मूल्यम् = price; औषधम् = medicine; ज्वरः = fever.
questions.explanation: Situation vocabulary from the shop and clinic model dialogues.

questions.question: From the doctor-patient model dialogue: what does भवतः का पीडा? mean, and what grammatical form is भवतः?
questions.answer: भवतः का पीडा? means 'What is your trouble/complaint?' भवतः is the genitive (षष्ठी, 'your') singular form of the respectful pronoun भवान् — literally 'of you, what pain (is there)?'
questions.explanation: भवान् → genitive भवतः; भवती → genitive भवत्याः.

questions.question: Write the लट्लकार (present tense) forms of the root पठ् in all three persons and three numbers, and then use any three different forms in short dialogue sentences.
questions.answer:
प्रथमपुरुषः: पठति (एकवचन), पठतः (द्विवचन), पठन्ति (बहुवचन)। मध्यमपुरुषः: पठसि, पठथः, पठथ। उत्तमपुरुषः: पठामि, पठावः, पठामः।
Dialogue sentences: (1) भवान् किं पठति? (What are you, sir, reading? — third person with भवान्) (2) अहं संस्कृतं पठामि। (I read Sanskrit.) (3) वयं प्रातःकाले पठामः। (We read in the morning.)
questions.explanation: The nine-form लट् table plus correct use in conversation, including the भवान्+पठति rule.

questions.question: Write an original Sanskrit dialogue of about 8 exchanges between two friends (मित्रयोः संवादः) planning to visit the library tomorrow. Use a greeting, at least two question words, one future-tense verb and a proper leave-taking.
questions.answer:
मित्रयोः संवादः
रामः — नमस्ते श्याम!
श्यामः — नमो नमः राम! भवान् कथम् अस्ति?
रामः — अहं कुशली अस्मि। श्वः किं करिष्यति भवान्?
श्यामः — श्वः अहं ग्रन्थालयं गमिष्यामि।
रामः — उत्तमम्! कदा गमिष्यति भवान्?
श्यामः — प्रातःकाले दशवादने। भवान् अपि आगच्छतु।
रामः — अस्तु, अहम् अपि आगमिष्यामि।
श्यामः — साधु! तर्हि श्वः मिलावः। पुनर्मिलामः।
(English: Two friends greet each other, ask about tomorrow's plan with किम्/कदा, fix a time to visit the library — गमिष्यामि/आगमिष्यामि future forms — and part with पुनर्मिलामः.)
questions.explanation: Any correct original dialogue is acceptable if it has the greeting, two question words (here किम् and कदा), a future verb (गमिष्यामि) and leave-taking, with भवान् always taking a third-person verb.

questions.question: Write an original Sanskrit dialogue of about 8 exchanges between a buyer and a seller in a fruit shop (क्रेता-विक्रेतयोः संवादः). Include a price question, one bargaining line, and courteous imperatives.
questions.answer:
आपणे क्रेता-विक्रेतयोः संवादः
क्रेता — नमस्ते महोदय!
विक्रेता — नमस्ते! स्वागतम्। भवान् किम् इच्छति?
क्रेता — कदलीफलानि सन्ति वा?
विक्रेता — आम्, नूतनानि कदलीफलानि सन्ति।
क्रेता — द्वादशफलानां कति मूल्यम्?
विक्रेता — षष्टिः रूप्यकाणि महोदय।
क्रेता — मूल्यम् अधिकम्। किञ्चित् न्यूनं करोतु।
विक्रेता — अस्तु, पञ्चाशत् रूप्यकाणि ददातु। गृह्णातु फलानि।
क्रेता — धन्यवादः महोदय। पुनः आगमिष्यामि।
(English: The buyer greets the seller, asks for bananas, asks the price of a dozen — कति मूल्यम्? — bargains with न्यूनं करोतु, and the deal closes with the courteous imperatives ददातु and गृह्णातु and thanks.)
questions.explanation: Any correct original shop dialogue is acceptable with the required elements: कति मूल्यम् price question, a bargaining request, courteous imperatives (करोतु, ददातु, गृह्णातु) and closing courtesy.

questions.question: State two layout conventions to follow when writing a संवाद in the examination.
questions.answer: (1) Write a title at the top naming the speakers or situation, e.g. मित्रयोः संवादः. (2) Write each speaker's name at the left followed by a dash (—) before their line, keep about 8-12 short exchanges, and begin with a greeting and end with leave-taking. (Any two.)
questions.explanation: Exam-layout conventions from the lesson's व्याकरणम् section (D).

questions.question: The word संवादः is formed from सम् + ____.
questions.explanation: सम् (together) + वादः (speaking) = संवादः, 'speaking together', a conversation.

questions.question: संवादलेखनम् is best described as
options: writing a conversation between two or more speakers
questions.answer: writing a conversation between two or more speakers
questions.explanation: संवादलेखनम् = dialogue writing, a composition skill.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT a quality of a good written संवाद?
options: long, bookish sentences full of rare words
a proper greeting at the start
questions.answer: long, bookish sentences full of rare words
questions.explanation: Dialogue sentences must be SHORT and natural, as people actually speak.

questions.question: In the exam layout of a dialogue, each speaker's line begins with
options: the speaker's name followed by a dash (—)
questions.answer: the speaker's name followed by a dash (—)
questions.explanation: Convention: speaker's name at the left, then a dash, then the spoken line.

questions.question: A dialogue should normally END with
options: leave-taking courtesy such as धन्यवादः or पुनर्मिलामः
questions.answer: leave-taking courtesy such as धन्यवादः or पुनर्मिलामः
questions.explanation: Open with a greeting, close with thanks or 'we shall meet again'.

questions.question: The recommended length of an exam dialogue is about
questions.explanation: About 8-12 short exchanges make a complete, well-shaped dialogue.

questions.question: Why is dialogue writing considered a bridge to संस्कृतसम्भाषणम् (spoken Sanskrit)?
options: it turns grammar into short, natural spoken sentences
it requires memorising long verse passages
it avoids the use of verbs altogether
it is written only in English
questions.answer: it turns grammar into short, natural spoken sentences
questions.explanation: Writing conversation practises exactly the forms one needs to speak.

questions.question: A dialogue between two friends should carry the title
questions.explanation: मित्रयोः is the genitive dual — 'of the two friends' — the standard title form.

questions.question: Which greeting can be used at ANY time of day?
questions.explanation: नमस्ते / नमो नमः are time-neutral salutations; सुप्रभातम् is only for morning.

questions.question: सुप्रभातम् means
questions.explanation: सु + प्रभातम् = good morning.

questions.question: The Sanskrit word for 'thank you' is
questions.explanation: धन्यवादः = thanks; स्वागतम् = welcome; क्षम्यताम् = pardon; अस्तु = okay.

questions.question: To say 'pardon me / excuse me' in a dialogue, one uses
questions.explanation: क्षम्यताम् = 'may it be forgiven' — pardon me.

questions.question: चिरात् दर्शनम् is said when
options: friends meet after a long time
questions.answer: friends meet after a long time
questions.explanation: चिरात् दर्शनम् = 'seen after long' — long time no see.

questions.question: The parting phrase पुनर्मिलामः means
questions.explanation: पुनः (again) + मिलामः (we meet) — the standard leave-taking.

questions.question: चिन्ता मास्तु means
questions.explanation: चिन्ता (worry) + मास्तु (let it not be) — 'don't worry', said by the doctor in the model dialogue.

questions.question: A guest arrives at your home. The natural word of reception is
questions.explanation: स्वागतम् = welcome — used to receive a guest or customer.

questions.question: The pair of words for 'yes' and 'no' in conversation is
questions.explanation: आम् = yes; न / नहि = no; अस्तु = 'all right', साधु = 'very good'.

questions.question: Your friend proposes: 'श्वः क्रीडाङ्गणं गच्छावः।' To AGREE politely you say
questions.explanation: अस्तु = 'all right/okay' expresses agreement; गच्छावः 'let us two go'.

questions.question: The respectful pronoun for addressing a MAN as 'you' is
questions.explanation: भवान् = you (m., respectful); भवती = you (f., respectful).

questions.question: To address a WOMAN respectfully as 'you', the pronoun is
questions.explanation: भवती is the feminine respectful 'you'.

questions.question: Although भवान् means 'you', its verb must be in the
questions.explanation: भवान्/भवती are grammatically third-person pronouns: भवान् गच्छति।

questions.question: Choose the CORRECT sentence.
questions.explanation: भवान् takes third person SINGULAR: गच्छति, not गच्छसि/गच्छामि/गच्छन्ति.

questions.question: Choose the CORRECT sentence with भवती.
questions.explanation: भवती, like भवान्, takes the third person singular पठति.

questions.question: With the informal pronoun त्वम्, the correct form is
questions.explanation: त्वम् takes the second person singular गच्छसि.

questions.question: The genitive ('your') form of भवान् is
questions.explanation: भवतः नाम किम्? = What is your (m.) name? The feminine genitive is भवत्याः.

questions.question: To ask a WOMAN her name respectfully, one says
questions.explanation: भवत्याः is the feminine genitive 'your'; भवतः is masculine.

questions.question: उपविशतु is a courteous way of saying
questions.explanation: उपविशतु — third-person courteous imperative of उप + विश् (to sit).

questions.question: The courteous imperative for 'please give' is
questions.explanation: ददातु = please give; गृह्णातु = please take; पिबतु = please drink; वदतु = please speak.

questions.question: Which pronoun choice suits a student speaking TO his teacher?
questions.explanation: Respect demands भवान् (or भवती for a lady teacher) + third-person singular verb; त्वम् is informal.

questions.question: Answering भवान् कथम् अस्ति?, a man says
questions.explanation: The speaker uses first person: अहम् + कुशली (m.) + अस्मि. A woman would say कुशलिनी.

questions.question: The question word कुत्र asks about
questions.explanation: कुत्र = where; कदा = when; कथम् = how; किमर्थम् = why.

questions.question: कदा means
questions.explanation: कदा asks about time.

questions.question: कथम् means
questions.explanation: कथम् asks about manner: एतत् कथम् अभवत्? — How did this happen?

questions.question: To ask 'why / for what purpose', the word is
questions.explanation: किमर्थम् = for what purpose, why.

questions.question: कति is used to ask
questions.explanation: कति = how many (number); कियत् = how much (quantity).

questions.question: The answer is 'अहं दिल्लीनगरे वसामि।' The question was
questions.explanation: The answer names a PLACE (दिल्लीनगरे), so the question word must be कुत्र.

questions.question: The answer is 'विद्यालयः दशवादने आरभते।' The question word needed is
questions.explanation: दशवादने ('at ten o'clock') answers a TIME question: विद्यालयः कदा आरभते?

questions.question: A yes/no question is formed by adding which word at the end?
questions.explanation: गृहकार्यं कृतवान् वा? — 'Have you done the homework?' — expects आम् or न.

questions.question: To ask the price in a shop, the buyer says
questions.explanation: कति मूल्यम्? = how much (is the) price? — as in एकस्य किलोपरिमाणस्य कति मूल्यम्?

questions.question: Which question naturally gets the answer 'आम्, कृतवान्।'?
questions.explanation: Only the वा-question is a yes/no question, answerable by आम् (yes).

questions.question: In the pair कः / का (who), the difference between the two forms is
options: कः is masculine, का is feminine
कः is singular, का is plural
कः asks about things, का about places
questions.answer: कः is masculine, का is feminine
questions.explanation: कः छात्रः? (which/who — m.), का छात्रा? (f.); both mean 'who'.

questions.question: Choose the question that CORRECTLY matches its answer.
options: प्रश्नः: भवान् किमर्थं विद्यालयं गच्छति? उत्तरम्: पठनार्थं गच्छामि।
प्रश्नः: भवान् कदा गच्छति? उत्तरम्: दिल्लीनगरे।
प्रश्नः: भवान् कुत्र गच्छति? उत्तरम्: दशवादने।
प्रश्नः: भवान् कथम् अस्ति? उत्तरम्: आपणे अस्ति।
questions.answer: प्रश्नः: भवान् किमर्थं विद्यालयं गच्छति? उत्तरम्: पठनार्थं गच्छामि।
questions.explanation: किमर्थम् (why) is answered by a purpose (पठनार्थम्, 'for study'); the other pairs mismatch time/place/manner.

questions.question: आपणः means
questions.explanation: आपणः = shop/market stall; the shop dialogue is आपणे क्रेता-विक्रेतयोः संवादः.

questions.question: The buyer and the seller are, respectively,
questions.explanation: क्रेता = buyer (from क्री, to buy); विक्रेता = seller.

questions.question: मूल्यम् means
questions.explanation: मूल्यम् = price; रूप्यकम् = rupee.

questions.question: ज्वरः means
questions.explanation: ज्वरः = fever; शिरोवेदना = headache; औषधम् = medicine.

questions.question: The word for 'medicine' is
questions.explanation: औषधं दिने त्रिवारं स्वीकरोतु — take the medicine three times a day.

questions.question: श्वः and ह्यः mean, respectively,
questions.explanation: श्वः = tomorrow; ह्यः = yesterday; अद्य = today.

questions.question: प्रातःकाले means
questions.explanation: प्रातःकाले = in the morning; सायङ्काले = in the evening.

questions.question: गृहकार्यम् means
questions.explanation: गृहकार्यम् = homework, as in गृहकार्यं कृतवान् वा?

questions.question: In a CLINIC dialogue, which set of vocabulary fits best?
questions.explanation: Fever, medicine and rest belong to the doctor-patient situation; the others suit shop, playground and school.

questions.question: रूप्यकम् means
questions.explanation: अशीतिः रूप्यकाणि = eighty rupees, in the shop dialogue.

questions.question: विश्रामं करोतु is advice most likely given by
questions.explanation: विश्रामं करोतु = 'please take rest' — the doctor's instruction in the clinic dialogue.

questions.question: क्षुधा नास्ति, said by the patient, means
questions.explanation: क्षुधा = hunger; नास्ति = is not — 'I have no appetite'.

questions.question: In the teacher-student model dialogue, the student addresses the teacher as
questions.explanation: गुरो! is the vocative of गुरु; the teacher in turn calls the student वत्स (dear child).

questions.question: In the friends' dialogue, कदा गमिष्यावः? uses the verb-form गमिष्यावः because
options: the two friends together are the subject — first person DUAL future
the sentence is in the past tense
questions.answer: the two friends together are the subject — first person DUAL future
questions.explanation: आवाम् (we two) → गमिष्यावः, उत्तमपुरुष द्विवचन of the future; likewise मिलावः 'we two shall meet'.

questions.question: In the shop dialogue, the buyer says किञ्चित् न्यूनं करोतु to
options: ask the seller to reduce the price a little
questions.answer: ask the seller to reduce the price a little
questions.explanation: किञ्चित् = a little; न्यूनं करोतु = please make (it) less — the bargaining line.

questions.question: The doctor's closing line शीघ्रं स्वस्थः भवतु means
questions.explanation: शीघ्रम् = quickly; स्वस्थः भवतु = may you become healthy.

questions.question: दिने त्रिवारम्, in the doctor's prescription, means
questions.explanation: दिने = in a day; त्रिवारम् = three times.

questions.question: In the friends' dialogue, अहं ग्रामं गतवान् आसम् expresses
options: a completed past action — 'I had gone to the village'
a future plan — 'I will go to the village'
a present habit — 'I go to the village daily'
questions.answer: a completed past action — 'I had gone to the village'
questions.explanation: गतवान् (having gone) + आसम् (I was) = 'I had gone' — explaining the friend's absence.

questions.question: Which feature is common to ALL FOUR model dialogues of this chapter?
options: they open with a नमस्ते-type greeting and close with courtesy
they all discuss the price of fruit
they are all set in a school
questions.answer: they open with a नमस्ते-type greeting and close with courtesy
questions.explanation: Greeting → question-answer body → courteous close is the shared skeleton.

questions.question: सायङ्काले पञ्चवादने, the meeting time fixed by the friends, means
options: in the evening at five o'clock
in the morning at five o'clock
on the fifth day of the week
questions.answer: in the evening at five o'clock
questions.explanation: सायङ्काले = in the evening; पञ्चवादने = at five o'clock.

questions.question: In the clinic dialogue the patient asks पुनः कदा आगच्छामि? and the doctor answers त्रिदिनानन्तरम् आगच्छतु। The answer means
questions.explanation: त्रिदिनानन्तरम् = after three days; आगच्छतु = please come.

questions.question: लट्लकारः denotes which tense?
questions.explanation: लट् = present; conversation happens mostly in the present tense.

questions.question: The first person (उत्तमपुरुष) singular लट् form of पठ् is
questions.explanation: अहं पठामि = I read; पठामः is plural (we read).

questions.question: वयम् (we, many) takes which form of पठ्?
questions.explanation: वयं पठामः = we read; पठावः is dual (आवां पठावः, we two read).

questions.question: ते बालकाः संस्कृतं ____। Choose the correct verb.
questions.explanation: Plural subject ते बालकाः takes third person plural पठन्ति.

questions.question: The vocative (सम्बोधन) of गुरु used in the dialogue is
questions.explanation: गुरो! = O teacher! — the सम्बोधन एकवचन of गुरु.

questions.question: भोः is used in conversation as
options: a general word for calling someone (O!/hello!)
questions.answer: a general word for calling someone (O!/hello!)
questions.explanation: भोः / भो मित्र! is a calling word used to attract attention politely.

questions.question: To respectfully address a LADY officer or teacher, the vocative is
questions.explanation: महोदय! = sir; महोदये! = madam (feminine vocative).

questions.question: युवां किं ____? (What are you two reading?) Choose the correct मध्यमपुरुष dual form.
questions.explanation: युवाम् (you two) → मध्यमपुरुष द्विवचन पठथः; पठथ is plural, पठतः is third-person dual.

questions.question: Forms like उपविशतु, ददातु and पिबतु belong grammatically to
options: लोट्लकार (imperative), third person singular — used for polite requests
questions.answer: लोट्लकार (imperative), third person singular — used for polite requests
questions.explanation: The courteous imperative pairs naturally with भवान्: भवान् उपविशतु — 'please (you) sit'.

questions.question: You must write a dialogue set in a LIBRARY. The most suitable opening line is
options: छात्रः — नमस्ते महोदय! किं संस्कृतपुस्तकानि सन्ति?
questions.answer: छात्रः — नमस्ते महोदय! किं संस्कृतपुस्तकानि सन्ति?
questions.explanation: Greeting + a books-question fits the library; the others belong to shop, clinic and playground scenes.

questions.question: A student's draft dialogue line reads: 'शिक्षकः — त्वं किं पठसि?' spoken by a STUDENT to the TEACHER. The best correction is
options: छात्रः should speak the line, and to a teacher he should say भवान् किं पठति?
questions.answer: छात्रः should speak the line, and to a teacher he should say भवान् किं पठति?
questions.explanation: Respect requires भवान् + third person; also the speaker label must match who is speaking.

questions.question: Which sequence is the best SKELETON for composing any new dialogue?
options: greeting → introductions/context → question-answer exchanges → courteous close
question-answer exchanges → greeting → title → grammar note
questions.answer: greeting → introductions/context → question-answer exchanges → courteous close
questions.explanation: This is the shared skeleton of all four model dialogues in the lesson.

questions.question: संवादः literally means 'speaking together' (सम् + वादः).
questions.explanation: सम् (together) + वादः (speaking) = conversation.

questions.question: सुप्रभातम् is the correct greeting to use at night.
questions.explanation: सुप्रभातम् = good morning; at night one says शुभरात्रिः.

questions.question: नमो नमः, like नमस्ते, can be used as a greeting at any time of day.
questions.explanation: Both are time-neutral salutations.

questions.question: The sentence भवान् गच्छसि is grammatically correct.
questions.explanation: भवान् takes a third-person verb: भवान् गच्छति। गच्छसि goes only with त्वम्.

questions.question: भवती is used to address a woman respectfully, and it takes a third-person singular verb.
questions.explanation: भवती किं पठति? — feminine respectful 'you' + third person singular.

questions.question: Adding वा at the end of a sentence turns it into a yes/no question.
questions.explanation: गृहकार्यं कृतवान् वा? expects the answer आम् or न.

questions.question: In the shop dialogue, क्रेता means the seller.
questions.explanation: क्रेता = buyer; the seller is विक्रेता.

questions.question: In the model dialogues, the doctor asks भवतः का पीडा? where भवतः means 'your' (genitive of भवान्).
questions.explanation: भवतः is the षष्ठी (genitive) of भवान् — 'of you/your'.

questions.question: The form पठावः is used when the subject is आवाम् (we two).
questions.explanation: उत्तमपुरुष द्विवचन: आवां पठावः — we two read.

questions.question: उपविशतु and ददातु are present-tense (लट्) forms.
questions.explanation: They are लोट्लकार (imperative) third-person singular forms, used as courteous requests.

questions.question: To thank someone at the end of a dialogue we say: ____। (thank you)
questions.explanation: धन्यवादः = thank you — the standard closing courtesy.

questions.question: To welcome a guest or customer we say: ____। (welcome)
questions.explanation: स्वागतम् = welcome, as the seller says in the shop dialogue.

questions.question: The parting phrase 'we shall meet again' is ____।
questions.explanation: पुनः + मिलामः = पुनर्मिलामः, the standard leave-taking.

questions.question: भवान् कुत्र ____? (Where are you, sir, going? — root गम्)
questions.explanation: भवान् takes third person singular: गच्छति.

questions.question: त्वं किं ____? (What are you reading? — informal, root पठ्)
questions.explanation: त्वम् takes second person singular: पठसि.

questions.question: ____ नाम किम्? (What is your name? — asking a MAN respectfully)
questions.explanation: भवतः = genitive of भवान् — 'your (m.)'; for a woman it is भवत्याः.

questions.question: विद्यालयः ____ आरभते? (WHEN does the school begin?)
questions.explanation: कदा asks about time.

questions.question: भवान् ____ वसति? (WHERE do you live?)
questions.explanation: कुत्र asks about place.

questions.question: एतत् ____ अभवत्? (HOW did this happen?)
questions.explanation: कथम् asks about manner.

questions.question: The Sanskrit word for 'shop' is ____।
questions.explanation: आपणः = shop; the shop dialogue is set आपणे (in the shop).

questions.question: The doctor gives the patient ____ to take three times a day. (medicine)
questions.explanation: औषधं दिने त्रिवारं स्वीकरोतु — take the medicine three times a day.

questions.question: ____ अहं क्रीडाङ्गणं गमिष्यामि। (TOMORROW I will go to the playground.)
questions.explanation: श्वः = tomorrow; ह्यः = yesterday; अद्य = today.

questions.question: अहं संस्कृतं ____। (I read Sanskrit — root पठ्)
questions.explanation: अहम् takes उत्तमपुरुष एकवचन पठामि.

questions.question: वयं प्रातःकाले ____। (We read in the morning — root पठ्)
questions.explanation: वयम् takes उत्तमपुरुष बहुवचन पठामः.

questions.question: The doctor says: उष्णं जलं ____। (Please drink hot water — courteous imperative of पा, to drink)
questions.explanation: पिबतु = please drink — लोट्लकार third person singular used politely.

questions.question: Break संवादः into its parts and explain its literal meaning. What is संवादलेखनम्?
questions.answer: संवादः = सम् (together, well) + वादः (speaking) — literally 'speaking together', i.e. a conversation between two or more people. संवादलेखनम् is the composition skill of writing such a conversation in Sanskrit, with greetings, questions and answers in short natural sentences.
questions.explanation: Word formation plus the composition-skill definition.

questions.question: List any four qualities of a good written Sanskrit dialogue.
questions.answer: (1) It opens with a proper greeting (अभिवादनम्) and ends with leave-taking. (2) Its sentences are short and natural, as people actually speak. (3) Questions and answers alternate in a logical flow (प्रश्नोत्तरप्रवाहः). (4) It uses polite forms — भवान्/भवती with third-person verbs and courteous imperatives — correctly. (Also acceptable: vocabulary suited to the situation.)
questions.explanation: Any four of the five qualities given in the lesson.

questions.question: State the layout conventions for writing a संवाद in the examination (title, speaker lines, length).
questions.answer: Write a title naming the speakers/situation at the top (e.g. मित्रयोः संवादः); write each speaker's name at the left followed by a dash (—) before the line; keep about 8-12 short exchanges; begin with a greeting and end with leave-taking such as धन्यवादः or पुनर्मिलामः.
questions.explanation: The four layout rules from section (D) of the lesson.

questions.question: Write the Sanskrit greetings for: (a) good morning (b) good night (c) any-time salutation (d) welcome.
questions.answer: (a) सुप्रभातम् (b) शुभरात्रिः (c) नमस्ते / नमो नमः (d) स्वागतम्
questions.explanation: The four basic greetings of the chapter.

questions.question: Write the standard 'how are you?' exchange between two men in Sanskrit (question and answer).
questions.answer: प्रश्नः — भवान् कथम् अस्ति? उत्तरम् — अहं कुशली अस्मि, धन्यवादः। (For women: भवती कथम् अस्ति? — अहं कुशलिनी अस्मि।)
questions.explanation: कथम् + अस्ति with भवान्; the reply uses first person अस्मि with कुशली/कुशलिनी.

questions.question: What do these courtesy words mean: अस्तु, क्षम्यताम्, साधु, चिरात् दर्शनम्?
questions.answer: अस्तु = all right / okay (agreement); क्षम्यताम् = pardon me / excuse me; साधु = very good / well done; चिरात् दर्शनम् = 'seen after a long time' — long time no see.
questions.explanation: Everyday courtesy phrases used inside dialogues.

questions.question: State the भवान्/भवती rule of verb agreement, and contrast it with त्वम्, giving one example sentence for each.
questions.answer: भवान् (m.) and भवती (f.) mean 'you' respectfully but are grammatically THIRD-person pronouns, so their verb is third person singular: भवान् कुत्र गच्छति? / भवती किं पठति? The informal त्वम् takes a second-person verb: त्वं कुत्र गच्छसि? Using गच्छसि with भवान् is wrong.
questions.explanation: The central politeness-grammar rule of the chapter.

questions.question: Give four courteous imperatives (लोट्, third person singular) used in the model dialogues, with meanings.
questions.answer: उपविशतु = please sit; ददातु = please give; गृह्णातु = please take; पिबतु = please drink. (Also acceptable: आगच्छतु please come, वदतु please speak, करोतु please do, स्वीकरोतु please take/accept.)
questions.explanation: Third-person imperatives express polite requests with भवान्.

questions.question: Rewrite these informal sentences respectfully using भवान् or भवती: (a) त्वं कुत्र वससि? (to a gentleman) (b) त्वं किं खादसि? (to a lady) (c) त्वम् उपविश। (to a guest)
questions.answer: (a) भवान् कुत्र वसति? (b) भवती किं खादति? (c) भवान् उपविशतु। (or भवती उपविशतु for a lady guest)
questions.explanation: Respectful rewriting changes the pronoun AND shifts the verb to third person singular (वसति, खादति) or the courteous imperative (उपविशतु).

questions.question: List the eight प्रश्नवाचक words of the chapter with their English meanings.
questions.answer: किम् = what; कः/का = who (m./f.); कुत्र = where; कदा = when; कथम् = how; किमर्थम् = why / for what purpose; कति = how many; कियत् = how much.
questions.explanation: The full interrogative set that drives dialogue flow.

questions.question: Frame a suitable Sanskrit question for each answer: (a) अहं दिल्लीनगरे वसामि। (b) अहं प्रातःकाले पठामि। (c) मम नाम रमेशः।
questions.answer: (a) भवान् कुत्र वसति? (b) भवान् कदा पठति? (c) भवतः नाम किम्?
questions.explanation: Match the question word to the information given: place → कुत्र, time → कदा, name → किम् with the genitive भवतः.

questions.question: How is a yes/no question formed in a Sanskrit dialogue? Give an example with its two possible answers.
questions.answer: By adding वा at the end of the sentence. Example: गृहकार्यं कृतवान् वा? (Have you done the homework?) — answered आम्, कृतवान्। (yes) or न, न कृतवान्। (no).
questions.explanation: वा is the yes/no tag; आम्/न begin the answers.

questions.question: Give the meanings: विद्यालयः, गृहकार्यम्, क्रीडाङ्गणम्, ग्रन्थालयः.
questions.answer: विद्यालयः = school; गृहकार्यम् = homework; क्रीडाङ्गणम् = playground; ग्रन्थालयः = library.
questions.explanation: School-situation vocabulary used in the dialogues.

questions.question: Sort these words into SHOP words and CLINIC words: मूल्यम्, ज्वरः, रूप्यकम्, औषधम्, विक्रेता, शिरोवेदना.
questions.answer: SHOP: मूल्यम् (price), रूप्यकम् (rupee), विक्रेता (seller). CLINIC: ज्वरः (fever), औषधम् (medicine), शिरोवेदना (headache).
questions.explanation: Choosing situation-appropriate vocabulary is a core dialogue-writing skill.

questions.question: From the teacher-student model dialogue, pick out: (a) one सम्बोधन (b) one yes/no question (c) one courteous imperative — and explain each briefly.
questions.answer: (a) गुरो! (O teacher — vocative of गुरु; also वत्स!, dear child). (b) गृहकार्यं कृतवान् वा? — the tag वा makes it a yes/no question, answered आम्. (c) सदा एवं करोतु — 'always do thus', a third-person courteous imperative used politely.
questions.explanation: The three politeness devices working together in one dialogue.

questions.question: In the friends' dialogue, explain the grammar of कदा गमिष्यावः? and तर्हि श्वः मिलावः। Why are these forms dual?
questions.answer: गमिष्यावः and मिलावः are FIRST-person DUAL forms (उत्तमपुरुष द्विवचन) — 'we two shall go' and 'we two shall meet'. They are dual because exactly two friends (रमेशः and सुरेशः) are the joint subject आवाम् (we two). गमिष्यावः is future tense of गम्; मिलावः expresses 'let us two meet'. तर्हि = then, श्वः = tomorrow.
questions.explanation: Sanskrit marks two-person subjects with special dual endings — natural in a two-speaker dialogue.

questions.question: Analyse the shop model dialogue: what is the buyer's goal, which line shows bargaining, and how does the deal close politely?
questions.answer: The buyer's goal is to buy mangoes (आम्रफलानि) at a fair price. Bargaining appears in मूल्यम् अधिकम् अस्ति। किञ्चित् न्यूनं करोतु। — 'the price is high, please reduce it a little' — and the seller yields from eighty to seventy rupees. The deal closes politely with courteous imperatives ददातु (give) and गृह्णातु (take), mutual धन्यवादः, and the buyer's promise पुनः आगमिष्यामि (I will come again).
questions.explanation: Goal → bargaining → courteous close: the structure of a market dialogue.

questions.question: Write the nine लट्लकार forms of पठ् in a 3x3 table order (person by number).
questions.answer: प्रथमपुरुषः: पठति (एक), पठतः (द्वि), पठन्ति (बहु)। मध्यमपुरुषः: पठसि, पठथः, पठथ। उत्तमपुरुषः: पठामि, पठावः, पठामः।
questions.explanation: The standard present-tense paradigm, the backbone of conversation.

questions.question: Give four सम्बोधन (vocative) forms used in dialogues, stating whom each addresses.
questions.answer: गुरो! — a teacher; वत्स! — a child/junior affectionately; महोदय! — a gentleman ('sir'); महोदये! — a lady ('madam'). (Also acceptable: हे मित्र! — a friend; भोः — general calling word; आर्य! — noble sir.)
questions.explanation: Vocatives open dialogue lines and set the tone of respect or affection.

questions.question: Choose the correct लट् form of गम् (गच्छ-) for each subject and write the full sentence: (a) सः विद्यालयं ____ (b) अहं गृहं ____ (c) ते बालकाः क्रीडाङ्गणं ____
questions.answer: (a) सः विद्यालयं गच्छति। (b) अहं गृहं गच्छामि। (c) ते बालकाः क्रीडाङ्गणं गच्छन्ति।
questions.explanation: Third singular गच्छति, first singular गच्छामि, third plural गच्छन्ति — agreement by person and number.

questions.question: Write a mini-dialogue of four lines (two exchanges) in Sanskrit between a librarian and a student who wants a Sanskrit book.
questions.answer:
छात्रः — नमस्ते महोदय! संस्कृतपुस्तकं किम् अस्ति?
ग्रन्थपालः — आम्, अस्ति। एतत् नूतनं पुस्तकं गृह्णातु।
छात्रः — धन्यवादः। एतत् कदा प्रत्यर्पयामि?
ग्रन्थपालः — सप्ताहानन्तरं प्रत्यर्पयतु।
(Student greets and asks for a Sanskrit book; the librarian gives it — गृह्णातु; the student asks when to return it — कदा; answer: after a week.)
questions.explanation: Any correct four-line dialogue with greeting, a question word, and courteous imperatives earns full marks.

questions.question: Convert this English exchange into a Sanskrit dialogue (two lines): Mother: 'Where are you going, son?' Son: 'Mother, I am going to school.'
questions.answer:
माता — पुत्र, त्वं कुत्र गच्छसि?
पुत्रः — अम्ब, अहं विद्यालयं गच्छामि।
(A mother may address her son with informal त्वम् + गच्छसि; the son answers in the first person गच्छामि. अम्ब/मातः = O mother.)
questions.explanation: Within the family the informal त्वम् is natural; the reply uses first person. भवान् कुत्र गच्छति? is also acceptable if respect is chosen.

questions.question: Explain the five qualities of a good written Sanskrit dialogue, and describe the standard exam layout (title, speaker lines, length, opening and closing). Why is dialogue writing called a bridge to spoken Sanskrit?
questions.answer:
Five qualities: (1) a proper greeting at the start and leave-taking at the end (अभिवादनम् — नमस्ते, धन्यवादः, पुनर्मिलामः); (2) short, natural sentences, written as people actually speak; (3) a logical question-answer flow (प्रश्नोत्तरप्रवाहः) in which every question receives a matching answer; (4) correct polite forms — भवान्/भवती with third-person singular verbs and courteous imperatives like उपविशतु, वदतु; (5) vocabulary suited to the situation — school words in a school scene, market words in a market scene.
Layout: write the title on top (e.g. मित्रयोः संवादः); each speaker's name at the left followed by a dash (—) and then the line; keep about 8-12 exchanges; open with a greeting and close with courtesy.
Dialogue writing is a bridge to spoken Sanskrit (संस्कृतसम्भाषणम्) because it forces the writer to turn grammar — pronouns, verb agreement, question words — into short living sentences that can be spoken directly; whoever can write a natural संवाद can also speak one.
questions.explanation: Qualities + layout + the connection to speaking practice.

questions.question: Discuss fully the grammar of respectful address in Sanskrit dialogue: भवान्/भवती with their verb agreement, their genitive forms, the contrast with त्वम्, and the courteous imperative. Support each point with an example.
questions.answer:
(1) भवान् (m.) and भवती (f.) are the respectful pronouns for 'you'. Though they address the listener, they are grammatically THIRD-person pronouns, so their verb is third person singular: भवान् कुत्र गच्छति? भवती किं पठति? Saying भवान् गच्छसि is a common error.
(2) Their genitives ('your') are भवतः (m.) and भवत्याः (f.): भवतः नाम किम्? भवत्याः गृहं कुत्र अस्ति?
(3) The informal pronoun त्वम् takes the normal second-person verb — त्वं कुत्र गच्छसि? — and is used with close friends, juniors and within the family; using त्वम् to a teacher or elder is impolite.
(4) Politeness is completed by the courteous imperative — लोट्लकार third person singular — for requests: भवान् उपविशतु (please sit), वदतु (please speak), ददातु (please give), गृह्णातु (please take), पिबतु (please drink). Together these devices let a dialogue show respect grammatically, not just through polite words.
questions.explanation: Four-part treatment of the politeness system: pronoun agreement, genitive, informal contrast, courteous imperative.

questions.question: Take the doctor-patient model dialogue and analyse it line-group by line-group: the opening, the complaint, the examination, the prescription, and the close. Point out at least four polite/grammatical devices used.
questions.answer:
Opening: the patient greets — नमस्ते वैद्यमहोदय! — and the doctor responds with नमस्ते and the courteous उपविशतु (please sit). Complaint: the doctor asks भवतः का पीडा? (What is your trouble? — genitive भवतः), and the patient reports ह्यः रात्रौ आरभ्य मम शिरोवेदना ज्वरः च अस्ति (headache and fever since last night). Examination: मुखम् उद्घाटयतु (please open your mouth) and the yes/no check भोजनं कृतवान् वा?, answered न... क्षुधा एव नास्ति. Prescription: reassurance चिन्ता मास्तु (don't worry) and instructions in courteous imperatives — औषधं दिने त्रिवारं स्वीकरोतु, उष्णं जलं पिबतु, विश्रामं करोतु. Close: the patient asks पुनः कदा आगच्छामि?, is told त्रिदिनानन्तरम् आगच्छतु (come after three days), thanks the doctor, and receives the blessing शीघ्रं स्वस्थः भवतु (get well soon).
Devices used: (1) respectful address महोदय and genitive भवतः; (2) courteous imperatives (उपविशतु, स्वीकरोतु, पिबतु); (3) the yes/no tag वा; (4) question word कदा driving the flow; (5) formulaic courtesy चिन्ता मास्तु and the closing blessing.
questions.explanation: A complete structural analysis showing how courtesy grammar organises a professional conversation.

questions.question: Compare the friends' dialogue (मित्रयोः संवादः) with the teacher-student dialogue (शिक्षक-छात्रयोः संवादः): how do tone, pronoun choice, tense usage and closing differ, and what does each teach a dialogue writer?
questions.answer:
Tone: the friends' dialogue is warm and equal — नमो नमः, चिरात् दर्शनम् — while the teacher-student dialogue is respectful and hierarchical — नमस्ते गुरो!, वत्स!
Pronouns: friends may still use the courteous भवान् (as in the model) or informal त्वम्; the student must use भवान् for the teacher, and the teacher may affectionately say वत्स. In both models भवान् takes the third-person verb (करिष्यति, पठति).
Tense: the friends plan the future — गमिष्यामि, आगमिष्यामि, and the duals गमिष्यावः/मिलावः — and recall the past (गतवान् आसम्, आसीत्); the classroom talk stays mostly in the present लट् (पठामि, पठति) with one past participle (कृतवान्).
Closing: friends part with तर्हि श्वः मिलावः / पुनर्मिलामः (we shall meet); the student closes with धन्यवादः गुरो! after the teacher's blessing-like praise साधु साधु and advice सदा एवं करोतु.
Lesson for the writer: match register to relationship — equal vs respectful — choose tense by situation (planning → future, classroom → present), and pick the closing courtesy that fits the bond.
questions.explanation: A comparative evaluation across tone, pronoun, tense and closing conventions.

questions.question: Explain why लट्लकार is called the backbone of dialogue. Write the full लट् paradigm of पठ्, and compose five short dialogue sentences each using a different form (include one with भवान् and one with a dual subject).
questions.answer:
Conversation mostly reports what is happening NOW — asking, answering, describing one's actions — so the present tense (लट्लकार) carries most dialogue lines.
Paradigm of पठ्: प्रथमपुरुषः पठति / पठतः / पठन्ति; मध्यमपुरुषः पठसि / पठथः / पठथ; उत्तमपुरुषः पठामि / पठावः / पठामः.
Five sentences: (1) भवान् किं पठति? — What are you (sir) reading? (भवान् + third singular). (2) अहं संस्कृतं पठामि। — I am reading Sanskrit. (3) आवां श्लोकं पठावः। — We two are reading a verse (dual subject आवाम्). (4) त्वं कदा पठसि? — When do you (informal) read? (5) ते छात्राः ग्रन्थालये पठन्ति। — Those students read in the library.
questions.explanation: Paradigm plus applied sentences covering the persons and numbers, including the भवान् rule and a dual.

questions.question: Compose an original शिक्षक-छात्रयोः संवादः (teacher-student dialogue) of 8-10 exchanges about the student's preparation for the coming examination. Use correct polite forms, at least three question words, one yes/no question with वा, and a proper opening and closing.
questions.answer:
शिक्षक-छात्रयोः संवादः
छात्रः — नमस्ते गुरो!
शिक्षिका/शिक्षकः — नमस्ते वत्स! भवान् कथम् अस्ति?
छात्रः — अहं कुशली अस्मि। परीक्षाविषये किञ्चित् पृच्छामि।
शिक्षकः — पृच्छतु। परीक्षा कदा अस्ति इति जानाति वा?
छात्रः — आम्, आगामिसप्ताहे अस्ति। अहं किं किं पठामि?
शिक्षकः — भवान् प्रथमं व्याकरणं पठतु, ततः संवादलेखनम् अभ्यसतु।
छात्रः — अहं प्रतिदिनं कति होरां पठामि?
शिक्षकः — प्रातःकाले द्वे होरे सायङ्काले च एका होरा पर्याप्ता।
छात्रः — अस्तु गुरो। संशये सति पुनः पृच्छामि।
शिक्षकः — अवश्यं पृच्छतु। साधु पठतु, सफलः भवतु!
छात्रः — धन्यवादः गुरो!
(The student asks about the exam using कदा, किम् and कति; the teacher checks with a वा-question; advice comes in courteous imperatives पठतु/अभ्यसतु/पृच्छतु; the dialogue closes with a blessing and thanks.)
questions.explanation: A model answer; any original dialogue with the required elements — polite forms, three question words, a वा-question, opening and closing — earns full marks.

questions.question: Compose an original चिकित्सक-रुग्णयोः संवादः (doctor-patient dialogue) of 8-10 exchanges about a stomach-ache (उदरवेदना). Include the doctor's questions, at least three courteous imperatives, and a closing blessing.
questions.answer:
चिकित्सक-रुग्णयोः संवादः
रुग्णा — नमस्ते वैद्यमहोदय!
चिकित्सकः — नमस्ते! उपविशतु। भवत्याः का पीडा?
रुग्णा — अद्य प्रातःकालात् मम उदरवेदना अस्ति।
चिकित्सकः — ह्यः किं भोजनं कृतवती?
रुग्णा — ह्यः अहम् आपणस्य तीक्ष्णं भोजनं खादितवती।
चिकित्सकः — तर्हि चिन्ता मास्तु। एतत् औषधं दिने द्विवारं स्वीकरोतु।
रुग्णा — भोजनविषये किं करोमि?
चिकित्सकः — अद्य लघु भोजनं खादतु, उष्णं जलं पिबतु, विश्रामं च करोतु।
रुग्णा — अस्तु महोदय। धन्यवादः।
चिकित्सकः — शीघ्रं स्वस्था भवतु!
(A lady patient — hence भवत्याः, कृतवती, खादितवती, स्वस्था — reports a stomach-ache; the doctor asks about yesterday's food and prescribes with the courteous imperatives स्वीकरोतु, खादतु, पिबतु, करोतु, closing with the blessing 'get well soon'.)
questions.explanation: A model answer; note the feminine forms (भवत्याः, कृतवती, स्वस्था) since the patient is a woman. Any correct original dialogue with the required elements earns full marks.

questions.question: Compose an original आपणे क्रेता-विक्रेतयोः संवादः (buyer-seller dialogue) of 8-10 exchanges about buying vegetables (शाकानि). Include a price enquiry with कति, one bargaining exchange, courteous imperatives, and closing courtesy on both sides.
questions.answer:
आपणे क्रेता-विक्रेतयोः संवादः
क्रेत्री — नमस्ते भोः!
विक्रेता — नमस्ते! स्वागतम्। भवती किम् इच्छति?
क्रेत्री — मम नूतनानि शाकानि आवश्यकानि। आलुकानि सन्ति वा?
विक्रेता — आम्, सन्ति। अद्य एव आगतानि।
क्रेत्री — एकस्य किलोपरिमाणस्य कति मूल्यम्?
विक्रेता — चत्वारिंशत् रूप्यकाणि।
क्रेत्री — मूल्यम् अधिकम्। किञ्चित् न्यूनं करोतु।
विक्रेता — अस्तु, त्रिंशत् रूप्यकाणि ददातु।
क्रेत्री — साधु। द्वे किलोपरिमाणे ददातु। एतानि रूप्यकाणि गृह्णातु।
विक्रेता — धन्यवादः। पुनः आगच्छतु।
(A lady buyer — क्रेत्री, भवती इच्छति — asks for potatoes, checks freshness, asks the price with कति मूल्यम्, bargains from forty to thirty rupees with न्यूनं करोतु, and both sides close with courteous imperatives and thanks.)
questions.explanation: A model answer; the required elements are the कति price question, a bargaining line, courteous imperatives (करोतु, ददातु, गृह्णातु, आगच्छतु) and mutual courtesy.

questions.question:
Read this dialogue and answer the questions.
छात्रः — नमस्ते गुरो!
शिक्षकः — नमस्ते वत्स! भवान् इदानीं किं पठति?
छात्रः — अहं संस्कृतं पठामि।
शिक्षकः — गृहकार्यं कृतवान् वा?
छात्रः — आम् गुरो, कृतवान्।
Questions: (a) Who are the speakers? (b) What is the student reading? (c) Which line is a yes/no question, and how do you know? (d) Why does the teacher say पठति but the student says पठामि?
questions.answer: (a) A teacher (शिक्षकः) and a student (छात्रः). (b) Sanskrit — अहं संस्कृतं पठामि। (c) गृहकार्यं कृतवान् वा? — the tag वा at the end makes it a yes/no question, answered आम्. (d) The teacher addresses the student with the respectful भवान्, which takes a third-person verb (पठति); the student speaks of himself in the first person, so he uses पठामि.
questions.explanation: Tests dialogue comprehension plus the two agreement rules (भवान्+3rd person, अहम्+1st person).

questions.question:
Read this shop exchange and answer.
क्रेता — एकस्य किलोपरिमाणस्य कति मूल्यम्?
विक्रेता — अशीतिः रूप्यकाणि महोदय।
क्रेता — मूल्यम् अधिकम् अस्ति। किञ्चित् न्यूनं करोतु।
विक्रेता — अस्तु, सप्ततिः रूप्यकाणि ददातु।
Questions: (a) What does the buyer ask first? (b) What was the original price and the final price? (c) Which words are courteous imperatives here? (d) What does अस्तु show about the seller?
questions.answer: (a) The price of one kilo — कति मूल्यम्? (b) Original: eighty rupees (अशीतिः रूप्यकाणि); final: seventy rupees (सप्ततिः रूप्यकाणि). (c) करोतु (please make/reduce) and ददातु (please give). (d) अस्तु ('all right') shows the seller agrees to the buyer's bargaining request.
questions.explanation: Reading numbers, the bargaining line and courtesy grammar in a market scene.

questions.question:
Read this clinic exchange and answer.
चिकित्सकः — नमस्ते! उपविशतु। भवतः का पीडा?
रुग्णः — ह्यः रात्रौ आरभ्य मम शिरोवेदना ज्वरः च अस्ति।
चिकित्सकः — चिन्ता मास्तु। औषधं दिने त्रिवारं स्वीकरोतु। उष्णं जलं पिबतु।
Questions: (a) What are the patient's two complaints and since when? (b) What form is भवतः and what does it mean? (c) List the three courteous imperatives. (d) How often must the medicine be taken?
questions.answer: (a) Headache (शिरोवेदना) and fever (ज्वरः), since last night (ह्यः रात्रौ आरभ्य). (b) भवतः is the genitive (षष्ठी) of भवान् — 'your': 'what is your trouble?' (c) उपविशतु (sit), स्वीकरोतु (take), पिबतु (drink). (d) Three times a day — दिने त्रिवारम्.
questions.explanation: Symptom vocabulary, the genitive of भवान् and prescription imperatives.

questions.question:
Read this friends' exchange and answer.
रमेशः — श्वः अहं क्रीडाङ्गणं गमिष्यामि। भवान् अपि आगच्छतु।
सुरेशः — अस्तु, अहम् अपि आगमिष्यामि। कदा गमिष्यावः?
रमेशः — सायङ्काले पञ्चवादने।
Questions: (a) Where and when do the friends plan to go? (b) Which verbs are in the future tense? (c) Why is गमिष्यावः dual? (d) Which courteous imperative appears, and what does it do?
questions.answer: (a) To the playground (क्रीडाङ्गणम्), tomorrow (श्वः) in the evening at five o'clock (सायङ्काले पञ्चवादने). (b) गमिष्यामि (I will go), आगमिष्यामि (I will come) and गमिष्यावः (we two will go). (c) Because the subject is आवाम् — the TWO friends together — so the first-person DUAL ending -वः is used. (d) आगच्छतु — 'please come (you too)' — a polite invitation using the third-person imperative with भवान्.
questions.explanation: Future forms, the dual, and the inviting imperative in a planning conversation.

questions.question:
A student wrote this dialogue. Find and correct its THREE errors, quoting the wrong words.
छात्रः — नमस्ते गुरो!
शिक्षकः — नमस्ते वत्स! त्वम् कथम् असि?
छात्रः — अहं कुशली अस्ति। भवान् किं पठसि?
शिक्षकः — अहं रामायणं पठामि।
questions.answer: Error 1: the STUDENT should address the teacher respectfully — शिक्षकः may say त्वम् to a junior, so त्वम् कथम् असि is acceptable from the teacher, but the polite model is भवान् कथम् अस्ति. Error 2: अहं कुशली अस्ति is wrong — अहम् needs the first person: अहं कुशली अस्मि। Error 3: भवान् किं पठसि is wrong — भवान् needs the third person: भवान् किं पठति? (Corrected dialogue: ...शिक्षकः — भवान्/त्वं कथम् अस्ति/असि? छात्रः — अहं कुशली अस्मि। भवान् किं पठति?)
questions.explanation: Error-hunting consolidates the three agreement rules: अहम्+अस्मि, भवान्+पठति, and appropriate register.

questions.question:
Read the ANSWERS below and reconstruct the missing QUESTIONS of the dialogue.
(?) — उत्तरम्: मम नाम गीता।
(?) — उत्तरम्: अहं जयपुरनगरे वसामि।
(?) — उत्तरम्: अहं द्वादशकक्ष्यायां पठामि।
(?) — उत्तरम्: आम्, मह्यं संस्कृतं रोचते।
questions.answer: (1) भवत्याः नाम किम्? (What is your name? — Gita is a girl, so the feminine genitive भवत्याः.) (2) भवती कुत्र वसति? (Where do you live?) (3) भवती कस्यां कक्ष्यायां पठति? (In which class do you study?) (4) भवत्याः संस्कृतं रोचते वा? / किं भवत्याः संस्कृतं रोचते? (Do you like Sanskrit? — a yes/no question with वा or किम्.)
questions.explanation: Reverse-engineering questions from answers: name → किम् with genitive, place → कुत्र, class → कस्याम् कक्ष्यायाम्, yes/no → वा.

questions.question:
The lines of this dialogue are jumbled. Arrange them in the natural order and justify briefly.
(1) विक्रेता — सप्ततिः रूप्यकाणि महोदय।
(2) क्रेता — नमस्ते! आम्रफलानां कति मूल्यम्?
(3) क्रेता — धन्यवादः। एतानि रूप्यकाणि गृह्णातु।
(4) विक्रेता — नमस्ते! स्वागतम्।
questions.answer: Natural order: (2) → (4) → (1) → (3). First the buyer greets and asks the price of mangoes (2); the seller returns the greeting and welcomes him (4); the seller then states the price — seventy rupees (1); finally the buyer pays, saying धन्यवादः and गृह्णातु (3). Justification: a dialogue follows the skeleton greeting → question → answer → courteous close, and only the seller can state the price, so (1) must follow (2) and (4), while the payment line with thanks (3) must come last.
questions.explanation: Sequencing exercises test the greeting → question → answer → close structure of a dialogue.

questions.question:
Read and answer.
प्राचार्यः — भवती किमर्थं विलम्बेन आगतवती?
छात्रा — क्षम्यताम् महोदय! मार्गे वृष्टिः आसीत्।
प्राचार्यः — अस्तु। श्वः समये आगच्छतु।
छात्रा — आम् महोदय, समये एव आगमिष्यामि।
Questions: (a) Why does the principal use भवती and आगतवती? (b) What does क्षम्यताम् do here? (c) Which line contains a courteous imperative? (d) What does the student promise?
questions.answer: (a) The student is a girl (छात्रा), so the feminine respectful pronoun भवती and the feminine past participle आगतवती ('came') are used. (b) क्षम्यताम् = 'pardon me' — the student apologises for coming late. (c) श्वः समये आगच्छतु — 'please come on time tomorrow' — आगच्छतु is the courteous imperative. (d) She promises to come exactly on time tomorrow — समये एव आगमिष्यामि (future tense).
questions.explanation: Feminine polite forms, apology courtesy, imperative and future promise in one scene.

questions.question: A dialogue is set in a विद्यालय (school). From the list below choose the FOUR words that belong to this scene and use any two of them in one short Sanskrit sentence each: औषधम्, कक्ष्या, गृहकार्यम्, मूल्यम्, पुस्तकम्, विक्रेता, शिक्षकः, ज्वरः.
questions.answer: School words: कक्ष्या (classroom/class), गृहकार्यम् (homework), पुस्तकम् (book), शिक्षकः (teacher). Sentences (any two): (1) अहं गृहकार्यं करोमि। — I do the homework. (2) शिक्षकः कक्ष्यायां पाठं पाठयति। — The teacher teaches the lesson in the classroom. (औषधम् and ज्वरः belong to the clinic; मूल्यम् and विक्रेता to the shop.)
questions.explanation: Choosing situation-appropriate vocabulary and using it in simple लट् sentences.

questions.question:
Situation: You (a student named अर्जुनः) meet your neighbour आन्टीजी-equivalent, a respected lady doctor (वैद्या), in the morning near the park. She asks about your health and your studies. Using the situation, WRITE the next SIX lines of the dialogue after this opening:
अर्जुनः — सुप्रभातम् महोदये!
वैद्या — सुप्रभातम् अर्जुन! ...
questions.answer:
अर्जुनः — सुप्रभातम् महोदये!
वैद्या — सुप्रभातम् अर्जुन! भवान् कथम् अस्ति?
अर्जुनः — अहं कुशली अस्मि महोदये। भवती कथम् अस्ति?
वैद्या — अहम् अपि कुशलिनी। भवान् इदानीं किं पठति?
अर्जुनः — अहं द्वादशकक्ष्यायां संस्कृतं पठामि।
वैद्या — उत्तमम्! प्रतिदिनं व्यायामम् अपि करोतु।
अर्जुनः — अस्तु महोदये। धन्यवादः। पुनर्मिलामः।
(The lady is addressed महोदये! and भवती + third-person अस्ति/पठति is used for her; she addresses the boy with भवान्; she answers with the feminine कुशलिनी; her advice uses the courteous करोतु; the close has धन्यवादः and पुनर्मिलामः.)
questions.explanation: Any correct continuation earns full marks if it keeps the masculine/feminine polite forms straight (भवान्/भवती, कुशली/कुशलिनी, महोदये vocative), uses a question word, and closes courteously.
